claim: In the matching retail DLL, seven small PlayerController_AI action-construction helpers called directly by FACT-0040 are closed as one wrapper family around the still-separate PlayerController_AI.SetAIAct core (0x06004F9D). SetAIAct_DownAtk (0x06004FA4) calls SetAIAct(raw 19, tm), stores aiActPrm=opt, and when is_wait_down is false stores aiActStep=1. SetAIAct_RunUpDive_Stand (0x06004FA2) calls SetAIAct(raw 9,512) then stores destCorner=corner; SetAIAct_RunUpDive_Down (0x06004FA3) is identical except raw action 10. SetAIAct_CornerDive (0x06004FA1) calls SetAIAct(raw 5,256), then stores destCorner=corner, nextSkill=dive_skill, and isLotPerformanceOnCorner=lot_perform. SetAIAct_PriAct_RunAtk (0x06004FAA) calls SetAIAct(raw 16,tm) then stores aiActPrm=kind. SetAIAct_GoGrapple (0x06004F9E) calls SetAIAct(raw 1,tm), stores nextSkill=skill and aiActPrm=dir. SetAIAct_GoBackGrapple (0x06004FA0) calls SetAIAct(raw 3,tm) then stores nextSkill=skill. FACT-0040 pins the exact eight direct wrapper calls at IL+0x00BF, 0x00E0, 0x012F, 0x013C, 0x01AE, 0x01F3, 0x022C, and 0x024B.
